units.text: INT. DOLLHOUSE - CONTINUOUS
. Mother, the stranger man has gone out through the gate.
units.name: THE CHILDREN

units.text: Yes, dears, I know. But, don’t tell anyone about the stranger man. Do you hear? Not even papa.
units.name: NORA

units.text: No, mother; but will you come and play again?
units.name: CHILDREN

units.text: No, no,—not now.
units.name: NORA

units.text: But, mother, you promised us.
units.name: CHILDREN

units.text: Yes, but I can’t now. Run away in; I have such a lot to do. Run away in, my sweet little darlings.
units.name: NORA

units.text: She gets them into the room by degrees and shuts the door on them; then sits down on the sofa, takes up a piece of needlework and sews a few stitches, but soon stops.
No!
units.name: NORA

units.text: Throws down the work, gets up, goes to the hall door and calls out.
Helen! bring the Tree in.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Goes to the table on the left, opens a drawer, and stops again.
No, no! it is quite impossible!
units.name: NORA

units.text: coming in with the Tree.
. Where shall I put it, ma’am?
units.name: MAID

units.text: Here, in the middle of the floor.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Shall I get you anything else?
units.name: MAID

units.text: No, thank you. I have all I want.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Exit MAID.
begins dressing the tree.

. A candle here-and flowers here—The horrible man! It’s all nonsense—there’s nothing wrong. The tree shall be splendid! I will do everything I can think of to please you, Torvald!—I will sing for you, dance for you—
units.name: NORA

units.text: HELMER comes in with some papers under his arm.
Oh! are you back already?
units.name: NORA

units.text: Yes. Has anyone been here?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Here? No.
units.name: NORA

units.text: That is strange. I saw Krogstad going out of the gate.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Did you? Oh yes, I forgot, Krogstad was here for a moment.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Nora, I can see from your manner that he has been here begging you to say a good word for him.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Yes.
units.name: NORA

units.text: And you were to appear to do it of your own accord; you were to conceal from me the fact of his having been here; didn’t he beg that of you too?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Yes, Torvald, but—
units.name: NORA

units.text: Nora, Nora, and you would be a party to that sort of thing? To have any talk with a man like that, and give him any sort of promise? And to tell me a lie into the bargain?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: A lie—?
units.name: NORA

units.text: Didn’t you tell me no one had been here?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Shakes his finger at her.
My little songbird must never do that again. A songbird must have a clean beak to chirp with—no false notes!
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Puts his arm round her waist.
That is so, isn’t it? Yes, I am sure it is.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Lets her go.
We will say no more about it.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Sits down by the stove.
How warm and snug it is here!
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Turns over his papers.
after a short pause, during which she busies herself with the Christmas Tree.
Torvald!
units.name: NORA

units.text: Yes.
units.name: HELMER
